title: How big is Africa, really?
hook: On most world maps Africa looks like one big country. Try fitting the giants inside it.

knows: that Africa is big on a map
that the US, China and India are large countries
doesNotKnow: that Africa's area exceeds the US, China and India combined
that the familiar map makes northern countries look bigger

misconception: Africa is about as big as one big country.
objective: The learner can explain that the US, China and India together cover only about three quarters of Africa's area (about 22 of 30 million km²), and that an equal-area map shows this while Mercator hides it.

claims.text: The US (lower 48 and Alaska), China and India together cover about 22.0 million km², about 73% of Africa's 30.0 million km², leaving about 8.0 million km².
claims.source: d3-geo geoArea x 6,371.0088² on the kit's 1:110m shapes, computed in Demo.tsx: US lower 48 7.98 + Alaska 1.48 (the US's two largest polygons; Hawaii and small islands, 0.04 M km², are not moved), China 9.41 (including Hainan), India 3.15, total 22.01; Africa = 51 shapes listed in africa.json, 30.04 (builder's node check, 2026-10-13). Published areas (CIA World Factbook: US 9.83, China 9.60, India 3.29; Africa about 30.4 million km²; from memory, not checked online) give about 74%. The lesson says 'about'.

claims.text: Moving a country across the globe by a rotation on the sphere does not change its size.
claims.source: Rotations of the sphere preserve area; place() in Demo.tsx composes d3-geo geoRotation calls (the kit's moveToLatitude uses the same method). Areas of the moved pieces are measured after the move.

claims.text: On an Equal Earth map, drawn areas are proportional to true areas.
claims.source: Šavrič, Patterson & Jenny (2018), The Equal Earth map projection, IJGIS 33(3) (cited in mercator-greenland, verified there). From memory for this lesson.

claims.text: The placement shown fits the three countries inside Africa with about 3% of the pieces overlapping a coast or each other; the fit is by total area, not an exact tiling.
claims.source: gen.mjs (committed alongside) searches rigid moves on a 0.5° raster of Africa; it reports the share of sample points outside Africa or on another piece (outsidePct in placements.json). The shown placement is one search result, chosen to illustrate the area comparison; the answer rests on c1, not on the placement.

claims.text: On a Mercator map the US and China, farther from the equator than most of Africa, are inflated more, which hides this.
claims.source: Mercator area scale sec² φ (Snyder 1987, ch. 7; verified in mercator-greenland c4). Centroids: contiguous US about 40°N, China about 36°N, Africa mostly within 35° of the equator. Not shown on this stage (no Mercator view); stated in the reveal.

claims.text: On most world maps Africa looks like one big country.
claims.source: Hook. A claim about common perception, after the misconception in the brief. No source; needs one (e.g. a survey of perceived country sizes) or softening.

recall.question: Which is bigger in area: Africa, or the US, China and India put together?
options: Africa, with about a quarter to spare
recall.why: The three cover about 22 million km², Africa about 30 million: they fill under three quarters of it.
